name: goja-493f2207-blind30-ots
instr:
# goja: a JavaScript engine misbehaving across the board, without a test suite

Embedding this JavaScript engine in a small host application and exercising it from script turns up a long list of wrong answers, and they are spread far apart. The repository has received 30 separate undocumented edits. Nothing about the language changed and nothing about the host side changed: script that used to come back with the right answers now comes back with wrong ones, and in several places an operation that used to succeed is refused outright.

The most visible trouble shows up with text handed in from the host side rather than written in the script. Joining two such pieces with the plus operator, or embedding them in a backtick-quoted piece of text, produces garbled output that does not equal the same two pieces run together by hand, while the identical expressions on script-authored text are fine. Asking where one such piece first occurs inside another gives nonsense rather than the expected offset or minus one. Asking where it last occurs is wrong too, and that wrongness spreads into padding and single-substitution calls that lean on the backward search. How long these pieces are, and their round trip out to serialized text and back, stay right. Removing a property from a bare piece of text misbehaves as well: removing an out-of-range position, an unknown name, or a punctuation-named key reports failure where all three used to report success.
